item.title: Former Michigan governors teaming up in ‘defining moment for civility’
item.description: Amid national tensions, former Michigan Govs. Rick Snyder, Jennifer Granholm, John Engler and Jim Blanchard are uniting in a bipartisan call for civil discourse.

item.title: Hundreds of miles of new transmission lines planned in Michigan
item.description: Michigan’s largest transmission company wants to build more than 350 miles of new high-voltage power lines across the Lower Peninsula in the coming years, starting with a 50-mile segment near Lansing. Company officials tout more reliable and cheaper energy, but neighbors are wary.

item.title: Scientists trying to solve mystery of ‘rock snot’ in Michigan streams
item.description: Didymo — also called ‘rock snot’ because of its appearance — suddenly bloomed in Michigan streams in recent years, and scientists don’t really know why.

item.title: Opinion | Don’t be fooled: The school smartphone bill won’t do much
item.description: If students have their phones in their pockets, the temptation to look at them in class will remain. The second issue is that allowing smartphones at lunch and in-between classes robs students of crucial face-to-face socialization.

item.title: Ypsilanti schools warn parents to take precautions amid reported ICE detentions
item.description: Ypsilanti Community Schools is urging families to make care plans and know their rights as reports of immigration enforcement by bus stop emerge.

item.title: Bridge Lunch Break recap: Experts call for tougher nursing home regulations
item.description: During a discussion Wednesday with Bridge readers, two experts called for tougher regulations and laws around nursing homes.

item.title: Unpaid medical debt? Michigan may soon limit how creditors can come after it
item.description: Unpaid medical debt is a national issue. A bipartisan pair of state senators hope to address repayment problems in Michigan.

item.title: Michigan cities limit salt use because icy temps mean it won’t work, anyway
item.description: Michigan cities are limiting road salt and prioritizing key routes as extreme cold reduces the salt’s effectiveness. Northern Michigan is seeing record snow totals, with some areas already above seasonal averages.

item.title: Michigan sees record cougar reports in 2025
item.description: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources confirmed 31 cougar observations in 2025 and the number is expected to go up. That doesn’t necessarily mean there are more cougars in the state, but at least one family is established here.

item.title: Hillsdale teams with Trump on US history. In divided land, not all are thrilled
item.description: Some content in the patriotic video series has drawn criticism, illuminating how difficult it is to portray the nation’s story at this moment in history, experts say.
